content.overview: BNS s. 287 — Negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter. Read with the chapter heading and neighbouring sections. A BNS provision with no single IPC predecessor. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 287 is the rule on “Negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter”. The section provides that whoever does, with fire or any combustible matter, any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any fire or any combustible matter in his possession as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from such fire or combustible matter, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 287 exists so that “Negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter” has a closed legal test in Chapter XV — Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Nuisance, adulteration, rash driving, obscenity, lottery.
